messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Latency SLO breach detected for streaming/generate on cluster us-west-2-gpu-pool-7. p99 > 2.0s over 5m window. Created INC-837654. Logs + traces: https://observability.redwood.internal/r/cluster/837654
alex (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming p95 ~180ms, p99 spikes ~2.1s. Start window ~09:12 UTC. Streaming stalls — clients see delayed final tokens.

alex (oncall): Quick snapshot: CPU decode workers at 92% on nodes 23-28, kv cache evictions up 3x. Prefill hit-rate dropped ~40% vs baseline.
dana: :eyes: Seeing slab fragmentation on those nodes. Metric: kv.slab_fragmentation[23-28] jump from 0.12 -> 0.67.
mike: Any 5xxs or dropped requests from customers?
alex (oncall): No widespread 5xxs. A handful of streaming timeouts logged (client timeout) and increased observability alerts for AcmeCorp and BetaApp traces.
seb: Stack traces point to long waits in decode path; worker threads blocked waiting for KV decode results. Prefillers not keeping the hotset warmed — likely shard imbalance + eviction churn.

ops-bot: Recommended immediate mitigations queued:
1) Scale gpu pool by +1 node
2) Increase streaming-proxy replicas +2
3) Temporarily route 10% traffic to model-variant-lite for non-enterprise routes

ops-bot: Running commands now:
```
# scale pool
./infractl pool scale --cluster us-west-2-gpu-pool-7 --delta 1
# bump streaming proxy
kubectl scale deploy/streaming-proxy -n prod --replicas=6
# route 10% to lite variant
./routingctl adjust --route /v1/generate --variant model-x-lite --pct 10
```

dana: Triggered a slab-compact on nodes 25 and 27 to defragment hot slabs. Also increasing prefill concurrency on those nodes from 4 -> 8.

alex (oncall): Executed restart of kv-agent on node-26 to force shard reallocation (rolling restart). Command:
```
ssh node-26 "sudo systemctl restart kv-agent && tail -n 200 /var/log/kv-agent.log"
```

seb: After the restart I can see prefill rate increasing on node-26. Prefill vs decode ratio moving from 0.45 -> 0.78 on that host. Good sign.
mike: How about a graceful fallback for long-running streams? Could we add a short keepalive to avoid stall detection triggering client timeouts?

alex (oncall): Added keepalive tiled heartbeats in streaming-proxy config; will roll to 50% canary then full. Patch: `streaming_proxy.keepalive_ms=10000`.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started for keepalive patch (50%). Monitoring latency heatmap: https://observability.redwood.internal/heatmaps/837654

dana: Noted a persistent shard hotset on shard-11. Prefill worker is starved because decode workers monopolize CPU. Plan: throttle decode concurrency on shards 11-13 to free cycles for prefill. Applying throttle now.

alex (oncall): Throttle applied: `decode.max_concurrency_per_shard=6` for shards 11-13. Watching metrics.

seb: Early telemetry looks promising — p99 down from 2.1s -> 1.1s within 6 minutes on canary. Streaming stalls decreased.

mike: Customer impact update: AcmeCorp experienced 2 degraded calls during window; BetaApp had increased tail latency but no errors. CS notified.

julia (next-oncall): I'm joining handoff in 10. Any open actions I should take when I take over?
alex (oncall): Handoff checklist for you @julia:
- Monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall count in the 837654 incident dashboard
- Keep the keepalive canary at 50% for 10m, then promote if ok
- Watch kv.eviction_rate and slab_fragmentation on nodes 23-28
- If stalls persist, trigger emergency route shift to model-x-lite 30% and open a capacity scale request
- Coordinate with infra to verify slab-compact completed on 25/27

julia (next-oncall): Got it. I'll take 09:30-11:30 UTC shift. Noted runbook link and will update INC-837654.

sre-lead: Thanks team — good mitigation steps. Follow-up actions for postmortem:
- root cause analysis: why prefill fell behind decode (profiling on prefill scheduler)
- evaluate shard rebalance heuristics to avoid hotset fragmentation
- consider adaptive prefill concurrency based on decode latency

incident-bot: Incident INC-837654 updated: severity -> SEV2, assigned to team eng-runtime. Handoff recorded: alex -> julia. :white_check_mark:

alex (oncall): handing off to @julia now. I'll remain available for 30m if needed. Summary: cache fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance caused decode backlog -> streaming tail spikes. Mitigations: scale +1, restart kv-agent (node-26), slab-compact 25/27, throttle decode on shards 11-13, keepalive canary 50%. Observed p99 improved to ~1.05s.

julia (next-oncall): Taking over. I'll post periodic updates in this thread and update the incident ticket. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incident-bot: Note: incident auto-escalation threshold not met. Will auto-close if p99 < 1.2s for 15m.
